title: The Coastal Wrestling Ground Where Waves Debate

features.name: the-weathered-boatshed
features.desc-on-touch: You run your hand along timber that has forgotten which way the grain once ran. Salt has rewritten it into something between wood and stone, patient and unbending.

features.name: the-fractured-stone-marker
features.desc-on-touch: A stone split by frost and argument, half-buried in shale. No name remains legible; only the white interior of the break, where something older meets the air.

features.name: the-listening-post
features.desc-on-touch: A rusted bracket holds the antenna upright, still broadcasting at 300 bits per second. Waves hit the shore in time with the carrier, or the carrier has learned to time itself to waves; you cannot tell which voice began.

features.name: the-tidepool-archive
features.desc-on-touch: Water that cannot decide whether it belongs to the ocean or the land, holding small stones, small shells, the occasional dissolved fragment of names that fell here over decades.

features.name: the-argument-carved-in-rock
features.desc-on-touch: Lichen has written its own grammar across the stone face: parallel lines, branching, loops that nearly close. It looks like argument, or weather recording its own passage.

inscription: the waves still speak in chorus; they debate without ears, without conclusion

file.name: Coastal_Chorus_1987_Spectral_Analysis.wav
file.note: A field recording of the argument between breakers and stone, 47 minutes, the carrier signal harmonizing with the water

exits.label: westward back through dissolving voices to where speakers learn to be many
northward along the headland where the coast curves away from itself
eastward out to where the horizon forgets the shore entirely
